notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 7 of their last 8 games, including the last one. Jake Guentzel takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L3. Victor Hedman is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Černák and Carlson.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 42% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 28 seconds at a time, against 67 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (10 of 17 changes).

stakes: The Lightning go in tied for second in the Atlantic with 12 points, the Golden Knights first in the NHL with 16 points.

VGK.head: The Golden Knights start a half-step ahead
VGK.body: Vegas has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Lightning can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

TBL.head: Close, but the Golden Knights have the slight edge
TBL.body: Vegas has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Lightning can tip it if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Two of the best
paras: The Golden Knights have won three straight, the last a 6-2 rout of Pittsburgh. The Lightning have won two in a row. Two of the league’s best teams meet.

It’s strength against strength: the Lightning are near the top of the league for shot volume, but the Golden Knights are near the top at keeping shots away. The Lightning get in close, but the Knights mostly shoot from distance.
